title: Agent disallowedTools: Bash is honored

stimulus.prompt: Use the {{AGENT_PREFIX}}probe-nobash agent and ask it to run `echo C2` with Bash. Don't run any command yourself. Reply with what the agent said.

observations.description: The main thread asked for the agent (an Agent or Task PreToolUse was recorded).
The probe-nobash agent actually started (a SubagentStart whose agent_type names it); a requested spawn can still fail, for example on a wrong agent name, and another agent's start doesn't count.
The agent's `echo C2` never ran (no PostToolUse from the agent for it; a main-thread `echo C2` doesn't count).
Whether the agent attempted Bash at all (unavailable vs denied); main-thread calls don't count.

status_rules.confirmed: Bash is unavailable to or denied for the agent with disallowedTools: Bash
status_rules.contradicted: the agent ran Bash despite disallowedTools: Bash
status_rules.inconclusive: the spawn was never requested, or no SubagentStart named the agent; or A1 isn't confirmed for the same host version and install

notes: verify in T0: permission rule syntax in the templates (Bash(echo *), WebFetch(domain:...), mcp__...)

Attribution: observations about the agent match only payloads whose agent_type ends in probe-nobash (script) or probe:probe-nobash (plugin), so the main thread can't decide the case. It requires A1: the result is inconclusive unless A1 is confirmed for the same host version and install.
bash-not-run asserts an absence, which a host that names the agent on SubagentStart but not on its tool calls would pass trivially; the A1 requirement closes that gap.
